A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, and the supplied pages are readable. V1 includes extensive supplementary proofs, implementation details, and experiments. V2 ends after its references while repeatedly referring to supplementary material that is not supplied, limiting comparison of those components.

before.justification: V1 reports original signal-fitting, image reconstruction, occupancy reconstruction, and NeRF experiments, including additional results in Section 7.

after.justification: V2 reports original optimization experiments, reconstruction comparisons, Hessian-sparsity measurements, and LLFF results in Figures 1-7 and Table 1.

M1.justification: V2 Section 5 introduces an infinity-norm ESGD-max variant alongside moving-average ESGD. V1 mentions moving averaging but does not describe this alternative. The underlying curvature-aware approach and AdaHessian(J/E) distinction remain.

E1.justification: The identified coverage remains 1D signal regression, DIV2K image reconstruction, Stanford shape occupancy, and NeRF on LLFF, with Blender and BLEFF still identified as supplementary evaluations. Additional LLFF scenes extend the existing benchmark rather than establish a new task or domain.

E2.justification: V2 adds SGD to the image-reconstruction optimizer comparisons in Figure 3a; v1's SGD comparisons concern occupancy and NeRF. The main multi-optimizer comparisons retain Adam, ESGD, AdaHessian(J), AdaHessian(E), Shampoo, and Kronecker/K-FAC. ESGD-max is described but not separately identified in the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Reported occupancy training data decrease from twelve million points to one million, and occupancy convergence plots switch from BCE loss to IoU. NeRF convergence plots also switch from PSNR to MSE, and LLFF evaluation expands from five to eight scenes. V2 specifies a 100-iteration preconditioner refresh interval; v1's main text says 50, but its appendix already says 100, so that difference does not establish an actual implementation change.

E4.justification: V2 adds a loss-convergence panel to the 1D conditioning analysis and extends activation controls, notably Adam-versus-ESGD comparisons for ReLU-PE against wavelet image models and sine occupancy models. The Hessian-sparsity analysis is retained: v2 Figure 4 redraws v1 supplementary Figure 7 with identical values.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Averaging Hessian-sparsity measurements across layers and training iterations was already documented in v1; its appearance in v2 is not new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds and revises convergence and reconstruction results across Figures 1-3 and 5-6. Table 1 preserves all five earlier LLFF rows and adds horns, room, and trex, each showing longer ESGD update time than Adam; for horns, the times are 227.58 versus 130.82 seconds. Figure 1 also adds explicit reconstruction measurements. Results under changed occupancy settings and metrics cannot establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 Theorem 4.2 explicitly extends the dense-Hessian-vector-product statement to sinc. Wavelet coverage is not new because v1's supplementary proof already includes it. However, v2 directs proofs to an unavailable supplement, while v1 supplies extensive derivations and proofs. The overall extent of theoretical and proof revisions therefore cannot be reliably assessed.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that curvature-aware preconditioning accelerates stochastic training for suitable nontraditional activations, explain Adam through diagonal Gauss-Newton preconditioning, and identify limited benefits for ReLU/ReLU-PE. V2 foregrounds the theoretical framework, but this contribution was already explicit in v1.

C2.justification: V1's limitations discuss the unresolved mismatch between improved condition numbers and faster convergence, including Jacobi's favorable image-training results. V2 replaces this with the unexplored possibility of better preconditioners for ReLU-PE. It also extends the higher-mode Hessian-noise interpretation to Shampoo alongside AdaHessian.

D1.justification: The code-access pointer changes from v1's Colab image-reconstruction demo to a source-code repository link in v2. However, v1 provides learning rates, initialization, preprocessing, ray sampling, and hardware details in its supplement, whereas v2 defers such information to an unavailable supplement. The full extent of reproducibility changes cannot be determined.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations including the sampling-theory work on activations, BANF, and Invertible Neural Warp. Some earlier mathematical references no longer appear in its reference list. The central positioning relative to neural-field activations, preconditioning, Adam, and earlier curvature-aware training remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, experimental narrative, and conclusion. It adopts neural-fields terminology, promotes notation into a main-text section, reorganizes Analysis as Theoretical Framework, and places the rewritten limitations before the conclusion.

P2.justification: V2 changes to a two-column layout and adds a prominent introductory figure. It redesigns convergence plots, combines the time and memory bars into a scatterplot, moves the appendix sparsity chart into the main text, separates occupancy curves from mesh illustrations, and expands the LLFF table.

improvement.justification: V2 makes activation-dependent behavior easier to inspect and provides a more balanced LLFF comparison by including additional cases where ESGD is slower. However, it drops the earlier condition-number caveat and defers central proofs and reproducibility information to an unavailable supplement. These presentation and reporting benefits cannot be reliably weighed against the changed qualifications and unresolved supporting material.
